My family has farmed this same land for three generations. I have about 12 mu. Around here, everybody grows winter wheat and then summer maize on the same fields — that is just what we do on the North China Plain. My father did it, my neighbors do it, the village agriculture office tells us to do it, and it works. I see no reason to change.

For the wheat, I will plant in mid-October after the summer maize comes off. I buy improved seed from the village supply co-op — the same variety most of my neighbors use, something like Jimai. Hybrid seed is too expensive and I do not fully trust it for wheat. I put down base fertilizer before rotary tillage, then top-dress urea at jointing. I water three times: once before winter to protect the roots from freezing, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in winter and a fungicide when the flag leaf comes out, because powdery mildew hits us some years.

For the summer maize, I plant straight into the wheat stubble right after harvest in June — no tillage, just push the seeds in and spray some herbicide. Hybrid seed is standard for maize, everyone uses it, the yields are clearly better. Summer rains usually carry the crop but I will run the pump once if August is dry. I apply urea twice, once early and once at the big bell stage. One pesticide spray if I see corn borer damage.

I expect around 480 jin per mu for wheat and 550 jin per mu for maize. Nothing fancy. Just steady.
